records.Concise description: The wallet built into Bitcoin Core, pairing local key management and transaction creation with a validating Bitcoin node.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Core includes wallet functionality inside the reference full-node implementation. New wallets are descriptor wallets, and the software supports watch-only configurations, PSBT workflows and external signers while using the user's own node for chain validation and broadcast. It is best understood as node-integrated wallet software rather than a lightweight consumer wallet.
Creators / founders: Satoshi Nakamoto — creator of the original Bitcoin software lineage
Bitcoin Core contributors — current maintainers and contributors
records.Launch / history: The original Bitcoin client launched in 2009; the Bitcoin Core project name emerged later as the reference implementation lineage. Version 31.1 was released in July 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Core is the canonical example of a wallet coupled directly to a fully validating Bitcoin node and establishes important reference behavior for descriptors, wallet RPCs and transaction construction.
Important technical or cultural characte: Self-custody software; private keys can remain local
Descriptor wallets are the current wallet model
Uses a fully validating local node rather than an SPV/indexer backend
Taproot-capable through current Bitcoin Core wallet/script support
records.Verification basis: Current Bitcoin Core release material, wallet RPC documentation and the official repository verify lifecycle and wallet capabilities.
Research notes / uncertainties: MSC should distinguish Bitcoin Core consensus/node behavior from optional wallet behavior.
Do not imply that running the wallet is required to run a Bitcoin Core node.

records.Concise description: A long-running open-source Bitcoin wallet using the Electrum server protocol, with advanced multisig, hardware-wallet and Lightning capabilities.
records.Deeper researched summary: Electrum is a lightweight self-custody wallet that avoids downloading the full blockchain by querying Electrum servers and verifying relevant transaction information with its lightweight client model. It supports cold/watch-only configurations, multisig, hardware-wallet plugins and an integrated Lightning implementation. Users can choose their own server, but server trust/privacy characteristics differ from running a full node locally.
records.Launch / history: Electrum was introduced in November 2011 and remains actively maintained; the 4.8.0 release line was current in August 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Electrum is one of Bitcoin's longest-lived independent wallets and helped establish lightweight deterministic wallets, hardware-wallet interoperability and the Electrum server ecosystem.
Important technical or cultural characte: Fee control and advanced transaction tooling
records.Verification basis: Current official site, documentation and repository/release material support lifecycle, platform and feature claims.
Research notes / uncertainties: Using a public Electrum server leaks more wallet-query information than querying a user's own infrastructure; privacy depends on server/network configuration.
Do not describe Electrum's lightweight verification model as equivalent to a fully validating Bitcoin node.

records.Concise description: A desktop Bitcoin wallet for detailed UTXO control, descriptors, multisig and hardware-signing workflows.
records.Deeper researched summary: Sparrow is an open-source desktop wallet designed to make Bitcoin transaction structure visible rather than abstract it away. It can connect to Bitcoin Core, private Electrum infrastructure or public Electrum servers; supports single-signature and multisig wallets; and integrates a broad range of hardware signers through USB, QR and file-based PSBT workflows.
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2020 and developed continuously as a Bitcoin-focused desktop wallet.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Sparrow has become a major power-user interface for coin control, multisig, hardware signers and transaction inspection, bridging self-custody hardware with private Bitcoin infrastructure.
Important technical or cultural characte: Extensive coin control and fee control
Hardware signers over USB and air-gapped QR/file flows
records.Verification basis: Current official feature documentation and repository verify wallet architecture and current operation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Backend choice materially affects privacy and trust assumptions; public Electrum use should not be presented as equivalent to a user's own node.

records.Concise description: An open-source desktop Bitcoin wallet and coordinator built around Bitcoin Core, multisig, PSBTs and hardware signers.
records.Deeper researched summary: Specter Desktop provides a graphical wallet layer over Bitcoin Core and related infrastructure, with a strong emphasis on multisig and external hardware signing. It builds and tracks wallet policies, coordinates PSBTs and supports QR, microSD and USB signer workflows. Its hot-wallet functionality has historically been secondary to its hardware-backed use.
Creators / founders: Stepan Snigirev — principal early developer and contributor
records.Launch / history: Developed from 2019–2020 onward as a Bitcoin Core-focused multisig and hardware-wallet interface.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Specter helped make do-it-yourself multisig and hardware-wallet coordination with a personal Bitcoin node substantially more accessible.
records.Verification basis: Current project documentation and official repository support its architecture and continuing project status.
Research notes / uncertainties: Specter DIY is treated as a related signer lineage, not a duplicate canonical profile.
Do not recommend or characterize experimental hot-wallet modes as equivalent to hardware-backed storage.
